correctness.rationale: Let A(n)=(-1)^n(E(n)−O(n)). The signed square-part product at −q factors exactly into a distinct-subset generating function for B={odd squares} union {2m²,m>=1}. Therefore A(n) is a nonnegative integer subset-sum count. Direct independent exact subset enumeration for ten allowed parts (1,2,8,9,18,25,32,49,50,72) gives total 266, 233 supported sums, an unbroken [65,201] interval, and exactly seventeen omissions <=64: 4,5,6,7,13,14,15,16,22,23,24,31,39,47,48,56,64. No omitted factor has size <=64, so low zeros are final. Adding 2m² for m>=7 propagates [65,T_m−65]; the integer intervals overlap when 2m²<=T_{m−1}−129, initially slack39 at m=7 and increasing by 2m²−4m−2>0. Since T_m diverges, every n>=65 is represented, without relying on finite extrapolation. Independent polynomial coefficient reconstruction to degree500 confirms the low exceptional set and positivity. The base exact finite premises plus symbolic all-m induction establish the unrestricted statement.
residual_risks: Only unrestricted partitions into positive squares, with empty partition at n=0; no statement about other powers.
